paragraphs.heading: A conversation with students
paragraphs.edited: Several years ago I was talking to a group of students, and I was explaining to them basically what's in 1 Corinthians 15. I was explaining the fact that without the resurrection, Christianity would cease to exist. It was once described to me that it's almost as if the resurrection were a tiny little thread connected to the fate of the world, and if we were to cut that thread, everything would fall apart. I was explaining this to my students, and the looks on their faces were priceless. You could tell that they didn't know anything I was explaining to them. It was all new news to them. They knew the resurrection. They were good Christian kids. They knew and believed that Jesus had resurrected, and they knew that it had something to do — or maybe everything to do — with their salvation.
